summary: Provision 'Cross-Org Initiative' Jira project template + Confluence space + Slack channel creation automation
description:
Issue summary:
Request to create a reusable cross-organizational initiative template that provisions three things in a single flow: 1) a Jira project (kanban backlog + standard issue types + lifecycle transitions), 2) a Confluence space using a standardized 'initiative' blueprint and page hierarchy, and 3) Slack channels (primary, #announce, #ops-support) with appropriate user groups and channel retention/pinning policies.

Impact:
Currently program leads spin up ad-hoc projects, resulting in inconsistent lifecycle workflows, missing runbooks in Confluence, and scattered Slack channels with no onboarding automation. This wastes time for platform and security teams and increases risk of undocumented workstreams. A template will reduce project setup time, improve discoverability, and enforce lifecycle and retention rules.

Request details / scope:
- Jira: create a project template called 'Cross-Org Initiative' with sample workflows (Backlog -> In Progress -> Review -> Done -> Archived). Include issue types: Epic, Initiative (custom), Task, Bug, Incident. Default components and labels. Default automation rules: when project marked 'Complete' transition all open tasks to 'Done' and schedule project archiving in 30 days.
- Confluence: create a space blueprint tied to the Jira template with recommended page tree (Overview, Goals, Roadmap, Runbooks, Retrospective). Auto-link the Jira project key to the Confluence space. Space permissions: view/edit restricted to project members and product/security leads; read access organization-wide.
- Slack: provisioning script to create #proj-<shortname>, #proj-<shortname>-announce, #proj-<shortname>-ops and associate them with an internal user group (proj-<shortname>-members). Default channel topics and pinned onboarding messages. Configure retention (90 days for #ops channel, 30 days for announce).
- Automation/orchestration: single entrypoint (Confluence form or Jira project creation UI) that kicks off the above provisioning steps. Provide rollback on failure and idempotency checks. Log actions to #internal-admin or a central audit Confluence page.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A new Jira project can be created from the template and contains the defined workflows, issue types, and automations.
2) A Confluence space is created and linked, with the status page showing the Jira project key and a starter page tree.
3) Slack channels are created with correct names, topics, retention settings, and group membership; onboarding message pinned.
4) A single UI flow (Confluence form or Jira create-flow) will perform steps 1-3 and return a success/failure summary.
5) Security review completed: permissions enforced, audit trail available, no external sharing.
6) Documentation added to Confluence runbook and an internal how-to for program leads.

Timeline/requested rollout:
- Prototype (POC) requested by 2026-03-26 for a limited pilot with two program leads.
- Pilot feedback window until 2026-04-09.
- General availability (GA) after review in the second week of April.

Stakeholders and approvers:
- Requester: Maya Singh (Program Ops)
- Engineering owner (automation): Jordan Kim
- Security reviewer: Priya Rao
- Platform/Tools owner: SRE Tools team (#sre-tools)
- Pilot users: Growth Ops (Elena Park), Data Platform (Arman Desai)

Risks / Notes:
- Need to confirm Slack API rate limits and workspace provisioning policy for automated channel creation. It's likely we'll need a service account with SCIM or admin scope.
- Jira project creation automation must be vetted to avoid accidental template proliferation. Consider quota per org/team.
- Confluence space permissions must be validated against existing org policies to avoid leaking restricted docs.
- This touches audit/retention policy; coordinate with Legal for retention durations.

Follow-ups / deliverables expected from implementer:
- Implementation design doc and proposed automation scripts (link to PR).
- Security checklist and audit log location.
- One-page user guide for program leads and a short onboarding video.
- Post-pilot checklist and metrics (time-to-provision, number of errors, support tickets created).
